newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stops aid to Tamil refugees.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stops aid to Tamil refugees.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Tuesday stopped giving financial aid to Tamil refugees in northern welfare centres and began issuing food instead in an effort to persuade them to return to their homes, officials said.
"We have stopped financial aid from today because we want to encourage them to go home," said a government official, who declined to be identified.
"More people are expected from the other side (Tamil rebel-held areas) in a few days," said K. Ganesh, the senior government administrator in the northern town of Vavuniya.
Some 15,500 Tamils lived in government welfare centres in Vavuniya, about 225 km (140 miles) north of the capital Colombo, he said.
"Many of them have been staying for up to six months," said the official. "Some appear to think they can stay on and have not decided to return to their homes."
Each family gets 250 rupees ($4.3) and individuals 50 rupees (85 cents) a day to buy food, he said.

"We cannot accommodate all of them so we are trying to encourage those already in the camps to return to their homes," he added. "It is so crowded that there is hardly enough room for people to cook."
Most of the people were displaced by fighting between government forces and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in the Wanni region last year.

The military said last week about 60,000 refugees had crossed to government-controlled Vavuniya since last October from rebel-held areas in the Wanni. It said 43,775 of the refugees had been sent to their homes in Jaffna and other parts of the north.
A military statement said on Tuesday that 724 people crossed over to government-controlled areas at Thandikulam, near Vavuniya, over the weekend.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the number is higher.
